correctness.rationale: The graph embedding is an isometry. Direct multiplication proves A_t B_t=I and all optimal absolute row sums. Coordinate-swap averaging reduces arbitrary projections to the equivariant class, whose first and third row sums satisfy L1 >= 1+h and L3 >= (1+t)(1-h) for every real h; the exact minimax intersection gives the universal lower bound. For interior t, strictness of |2t-1|<1 forces d=0 at equality and hence uniqueness of the symmetric optimizer. The real Banach–Mazur bound is obtained from an explicitly contractive 2-by-2 transform and its exact inverse norm. Ten exact rational parameter checks were successful; the full continuum follows from algebraic inequalities, not tests. Independent verification is unperformed.

value.rationale: Absolute projection constants measure intrinsic injectivity defects. This canonical four-coordinate, exchange-symmetric codimension-two family interpolates between the injective real square and the uniquely extremal affine-regular hexagon, and the new formula measures that defect at every intermediate octagonal stage. A sharp explicit projection and equivariant rigidity explain the optimal cost, while the exact first-order Banach–Mazur behavior supplies a distinct local stability consequence. The object and invariant are mathematically natural and are not an arbitrary numerical slice or an endpoint recomputation.
